field.label: Enable
field.help: Map each address to its user - from the domain controllers' logon events, RADIUS accounting and the captive portal's sessions, as chosen here - and fill the tables of the group and user rows. Off by default: nothing is mapped until a source is chosen and groups or users are named. Off, every mapping is forgotten and the plugin's aliases leave Firewall: Aliases - switched off instead where a rule or a setting still names one.

field.label: Domain controllers
field.help: The IPv4 addresses of the domain controllers that send their logon events, with NXLog CE (Sources shows its configuration). Only these are let in: pf redirects their port to syslog-ng on 127.0.0.1, and a line from any other address is never read.

field.label: Interfaces
field.help: Where the domain controllers' events come in.

field.label: Port
field.help: The TCP port the domain controllers send to, on the firewall's addresses. Not one the firewall itself serves - SSH, DNS, the web GUI on 80, 443 or its own port: the domain controllers would no longer reach that service.

field.label: RADIUS accounting
field.help: Map the address of each RADIUS session to its user, from the accounting os-freeradius writes as each request comes: a Start maps its Framed-IP-Address, an Interim-Update renews it, a Stop takes it out. A NAS - or another RADIUS server that forwards its accounting - must be a client of Services: FreeRADIUS. A NAS that sends no Interim-Update leaves the mapping to the end of its lifetime, even while the session goes on.

field.label: Captive portal sessions
field.help: Map the address of each session of the captive portal to the user that logged on, from the logon to the logout or the portal's own timeout - read every two seconds from the portal's database. The sessions of allowed addresses, of vouchers and of zones with no login map nothing.

field.label: Groups from
field.help: The LDAP entry of System: Access: Servers asked which groups a user is in. Active Directory refuses a bind in the clear: StartTLS or SSL, with the domain's certificate authority in System: Trust and the domain controller named as its certificate names it.

field.label: Nested groups (Active Directory)
field.help: A user in a group that is inside a chosen group counts as in it: Active Directory is asked by its in-chain rule, one question a group. A server that does not know the rule is asked memberOf alone.

field.label: Mapping lifetime (minutes)
field.help: How long an address stays mapped with no event about it. A domain controller says nothing when a user logs off or locks the screen, so this is what ends a mapping, besides another user's logon from the same address. An idle session renews itself: the network logons it makes keep coming.

field.label: Drop when the address's MAC changes
field.help: Every minute, an address whose MAC in the firewall's ARP or neighbour table is not the one it had leaves the map: another device has it. Behind a router the firewall sees no MAC, and only the lifetime ends a mapping.

field.label: Stale after (minutes)
field.help: An event older than this when it arrives neither maps nor renews: NXLog CE sends again what it held while stopped. Counted as stale on Sources. The events' times are read in the firewall's time zone: the domain controllers must keep the same zone, and a close clock.

field.label: Never map
field.help: Addresses and networks never mapped to a user: terminal servers, NAT inside the network, servers that log on to the domain controllers as a user. The firewall's own addresses and the domain controllers' never are.

field.label: Ignore users
field.help: Users never mapped: service accounts, administrators logging on to servers.

field.label: Log user names
field.help: The system log says how many addresses were mapped, changed user or left. On, it names each address and its user, and so do the alerts.

field.label: Keep history (days)
field.help: Each mapping made, changed or ended, kept a file a day in /var/db/os-useridentity/history for this many days. 0: none is kept, only the live map.

field.label: Alert when a domain controller is silent (minutes)
field.help: 0: no alert. An alert is a file in /var/db/os-useridentity/alerts, in os-xgs-npu's form, for os-netreport to send; the directory failing and an address newly shared are alerted too.

field.label: Local port
field.help: The port of syslog-ng's source on 127.0.0.1 that the domain controllers' lines are redirected to; 5140 is os-xgs-npu's. It is written only when no other program holds it: a source that cannot be bound would stop syslog-ng, and every log with it.
